name: parse-error
documentation:
A Python file in the workspace cannot be parsed.

No other rule can check a file that does not parse, so this finding hides
nothing: fix the syntax error and run the check again.

name: unclassified-file
documentation:
A Python file matches no layer.

Every file in a package must belong to exactly one layer, because the other
rules are defined per layer. Move the file to a path the package layout
recognizes, extend the layout in `[layouts.<name>]`, or add an `[[overrides]]`
entry with a reason and an issue.

name: manifest
documentation:
`lint-it.toml` is invalid or out of date with the workspace.

Reported at `lint-it.toml:1` for schema errors, unknown keys, overrides that
no longer match any file, overlapping overrides, and exceeded override
budgets. A manifest that cannot be loaded at all exits with status 2.

name: layer-dependency
documentation:
A module imports a layer its own layer may not depend on.

The allowed targets per layer come from `[layer_dependencies]`; by default
core and port import only core and port, shell adds shell, adapter adds
adapter, and routers import shell, boundary, router and transaction modules.
Other layers are unrestricted, except that only test code may import test
code, so a composition root cannot wire a fake into production. A custom
layer uses its base layer's entry unless it has its own, and counts as its
base layer when imported. Imports are followed through package `__init__`
modules and re-exports, so a package initializer cannot launder a forbidden
dependency. Each forbidden module is reported once per importer. Declare
modules a layer may always use with `[[allowed_dependencies]]`, or record
one deliberate edge with `[[dependency_overrides]]`.

name: forbidden-import
documentation:
A module imports a third-party package its layer may not use.

By default core and port modules may not import I/O clients (`httpx`,
`requests`, `redis`, `sqlite3`, `subprocess`, ...) or frameworks (`fastapi`,
`starlette`, `sqlalchemy`, `pydantic`, `pydantic_settings`); shell modules
may not import frameworks; routers may not import `sqlalchemy`. Set
`[forbidden_imports]` to replace a layer's list, or
`[extend_forbidden_imports]` to add to it. Every import statement counts,
including deferred and `TYPE_CHECKING` ones, and a workspace module that
re-exports a forbidden name is treated as that package.

name: client-imports-server
documentation:
A client package imports a server package from the same workspace.

Packages with `kind = "client"` (SDKs, wire contracts) ship to consumers that
do not have the server installed. They may import libraries and other
clients, never modules owned by a `kind = "server"` package.

name: cross-domain-import
documentation:
A domain imports another domain it does not declare, or that domain's internals.

A module under `<package>/domains/<name>/` belongs to domain `<name>`. It may
import another domain only when `[domains]` lists that domain among its
dependencies, and then only its core and shell modules (`core.py`,
`model.py`, `service.py`, ...); ports, adapters such as `persistence/`, and
boundaries stay private to their domain. Undeclared imports always fail,
so a workspace without `[domains]` keeps its domains independent. The
graph is checked when the manifest loads: every domain a dependency names
needs its own entry, and a cycle is a manifest error. `shared/`,
`projections/` and everything outside `domains/` are not domains. Imports
are followed through package `__init__` modules and re-exports, as for
LIT101, and `[[dependency_overrides]]` exempts one deliberate edge.

name: nondeterminism
documentation:
Code reads the clock, randomness, or fresh IDs directly.

Core and port modules may not read any nondeterministic source (`time`,
`datetime.now`, `uuid4`, `random`, `secrets`, `os.urandom`); pass the
observed value in. Elsewhere only wall-clock reads are reported, so time
flows through one clock you can control in tests. List that clock's modules
in `workspace.clock_modules`; test modules are exempt. A custom layer with
`deterministic = true`, such as Temporal workflow code, is held to the core
standard.

name: io-in-core
documentation:
Core or port code performs I/O.

Covers files and paths (`open`, `Path.read_text`, `shutil`, `tempfile`),
processes and the OS (`os.system`, `sys.exit`), standard streams, logging,
`print`/`input`, and any call into an I/O client package. Do the I/O in the
shell and pass the result into the core.

name: ambient-state
documentation:
Core or port code reads or writes state it was not given.

Reports process-wide context (working directory, locale, decimal context,
context variables), writes through `global`/`nonlocal`, and reads of
mutable module-level collections. Pass the value in and return the new
state instead. Environment variables are covered by LIT301.

name: borrowed-mutation
documentation:
Core or port code mutates a value it received as an argument.

Tracks parameters, and aliases of them, through assignment, item and
attribute stores, `del`, augmented assignment, and mutating methods of
lists, dicts and sets. Build and return a new value instead; the caller
owns what it passed in.

name: frozen-values
documentation:
A core or port dataclass is mutable.

Dataclasses must be declared with `frozen=True`, and their fields may not be
annotated with mutable collections (`list`, `dict`, `set`, or the `typing`
and `collections.abc` mutable protocols). `ClassVar` fields are exempt. Use
tuples, frozensets, or read-only `Mapping`/`Sequence` interfaces.

name: async-in-core
documentation:
Core code awaits or schedules concurrent work.

`await`, `async for`, `async with`, `asyncio` scheduling, threads and process
pools belong in the shell. The core computes a decision from values; the
shell decides when and how concurrently to carry it out.

name: effectful-capability
documentation:
A core function takes a parameter that can perform effects.

Database sessions and connections, HTTP clients, file objects and
filesystems are capabilities: a function that receives one can do I/O even
when it imports nothing. Types are matched by exact resolved name, through
aliases, unions, `Optional`, `Annotated` and string annotations. Add your own
with `workspace.effectful_types`. Ports are exempt because they describe
effectful collaborators.

name: environment-access
documentation:
Code outside the edges reads environment variables.

`os.environ`, `os.getenv` and their bytes variants, through any alias, are
allowed only in boundary, transaction and test modules. Read configuration
once at startup and pass typed values inward.

name: transaction-boundary
documentation:
Code outside a transaction boundary calls `commit()` or `rollback()`.

One place per request or job decides when work is durable. Any method named
`commit` or `rollback` counts, on any receiver; only transaction and test
modules may call them.

name: router-construction
documentation:
A router constructs its own infrastructure.

Routers receive repositories, clients, engines and settings through
dependency injection; they never build them. Calls to anything named
`*Repository`, `*Client` or `*Engine`, `create_engine`,
`create_async_engine` or `load_settings` are reported, matched by resolved
name when the import is known.

name: mocking
documentation:
A test patches code instead of passing fakes in.

Reports `unittest.mock`, pytest-mock fixtures (`mocker` and friends) and
`monkeypatch` methods in test modules. If a test needs to replace a
collaborator, the code under test should accept it as a port; pass a
hand-written fake that implements it.

name: immutable-defaults
documentation:
A parameter default is not an immutable value.

Outside the edge layers (boundary, router, transaction, test), defaults may
only be literals, signed numbers, tuples, `UPPER_CASE` constants and enum
members, and immutable constructors such as `frozenset()` or `Decimal("0")`
over those. A same-module constant bound to a mutable value still counts as
mutable. A default such as
`[]`, `Settings()` or `datetime.now()` is evaluated once at import time and
hides a dependency; make the caller pass it. Protocol methods and exception
`__init__` methods are exempt.

name: forbidden-call
documentation:
A module calls a function its layer may not call.

Nothing is forbidden by default. List qualified names per layer in
`[forbidden_calls]`, with a trailing `.*` for a whole module: for example
`time.sleep` and `asyncio.sleep` in Temporal workflow code, which must use
the workflow's own timer. Calls are matched by resolved name, so aliases
and `from` imports count. A custom layer inherits its base layer's list
unless it has its own.

name: boolean-policy
documentation:
A public core function takes a boolean, or returns one without a predicate name.

A `bool` parameter is a hidden mode switch; replace it with an enum or a
named value type. A function returning `bool` must be named as a question,
with one of the prefixes in `conventions.predicate_prefixes` (default `is_`,
`has_`, `can_`, `should_`, `allows_`, `contains_`, `matches_`). Private
functions are exempt.

name: expected-outcome
documentation:
Core code raises or catches an expected outcome.

"Not found", "denied" or "expired" are ordinary results of a decision, not
failures. Exceptions whose names end with a suffix from
`conventions.outcome_suffixes` (default `NotFound`, `AlreadyExists`,
`Conflict`, `Denied`, `Expired`, `Forbidden`, `Rejected`, `Unauthorized`,
`Unavailable`) may not be raised or caught in core modules; return a named
result type instead.

name: restricted-subclassing
documentation:
A class extends a base that is not on the allowlist.

Inheritance couples a class to its parent's internals; prefer composition,
functions over values, and `Protocol`s for shared interfaces. A class may
extend a name in `conventions.allowed_bases` (default: every builtin, such
as `Exception`, plus `typing.Protocol`/`NamedTuple`/`TypedDict`/`Generic`,
`enum` bases, Pydantic `BaseModel`/`RootModel`/`BaseSettings`, and
SQLAlchemy declarative bases and `TypeDecorator`), or a workspace class that
directly extends one: a shared `Base(DeclarativeBase)` for tables, a common
`Model(BaseModel)`, a `DomainError(Exception)`, or a `Protocol` a fake
implements. Deeper hierarchies are reported, except for exceptions, which
may nest to any depth. A table that extends a declarative base may also mix
in plain workspace classes, such as a `ProjectOwned` holding shared columns.
Entries ending in `.*` allow a whole module. Set `conventions.allowed_bases`
to replace the list, or `conventions.extend_allowed_bases` to add to it.
